simple.meaning: אָרַח (ʼârach) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to travel.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in Judges, 2 Samuel, Job, Jeremiah, beginning at Judges 19:17. The surrounding contexts include flock, city, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָרַח (H732) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָרַח (ʼârach) / H732 is traced through Judges 19:17, 2 Samuel 12:4, Job 34:8, Jeremiah 9:1 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H732. arach אָרַח verb wander, journey, go (Phoenician ארךְ in מארח , probably = מְאָרֵחַ compare Ethiopic lead, conduct , see Nö ZMG 1888, 472 ; epithet of god Eshmun, Sabean ארחֿ DHM Epigr. Denkm. p. 70 , Aramaic אוֺרֵחַ , traveller ) — Qal Perfect וְאָרַה consecutive Job 34:8 ; Participle אֹרֵחַ Judg 19:17 +; plural אֹרְהִים Jer 9:1 ; — 1 journey, go , with עִם figurative of association, companionship Job 34:8 ׳וְא עִםאַֿנְשֵׁיֶֿרשַׁע׃ וְלָלֶכֶת אָ֑וֶן עִםמֹּֿעֲלֵי לְחֶבְרָה (compare also הלך Psa 1:1 ). 2 Participle wandering, wayfaring, journeying , הָאֹרֵחַ הָאִישׁ Judg 19:17 ; as substantive wanderer, wayfarer, traveller אֹרֵחַ 2Sam 12:4 (|| הֵלֶךְ ), Jer 14:8 (|| גֵּר , in simile of ׳י ); אֹרְחִים מְלוֺן wayfarers' lodging-place 9:1 .

occurrences.englishText: He lifted up his eyes, and saw the wayfaring man in the street of the city; and the old man said, “Where are you going? Where did you come from?”

A traveler came to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to prepare for the wayfaring man who had come to him, but took the poor man’s lamb, and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”
Who goes in company with the workers of iniquity,
Oh that my head were waters,
